findings.title: Missing re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: `GetWebAssets` reads the cache under `RLock`, releases it, and then takes the write lock without re-checking whether another goroutine populated `entryPointAssetsCache` in the meantime (classic double-checked-locking recheck). Consequence: on startup, if N requests arrive concurrently with an empty cache, all N serialize on the write lock and each one re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` (or performs a CDN HTTP fetch) even though the first one already produced a valid result. In addition, every one of those late writers overwrites the already-published pointer; if a later read fails (file transiently unavailable, CDN error) the code unconditionally executes `entryPointAssetsCache = result` with `result == nil`, discarding a previously valid cached value and making subsequent callers re-do the work / receive `nil`. Adding `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` right after `Lock()`, and only assigning the cache when `err == nil`, fixes both.

findings.title: Cache is overwritten with nil when manifest loading fails
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is executed unconditionally, including when `err != nil` and `result == nil`. This makes a load failure poison/clear the cache rather than leaving the last known-good assets in place, so every later request repeats the failing file/CDN read and callers get a nil `*dtos.EntryPointAssets`. Guard the assignment with `if err == nil && result != nil`.

findings.title: No test covering the concurrent access the PR claims to fix
findings.body: The PR is specifically a data-race fix on the `entryPointAssetsCache` global, but no test was added that exercises `GetWebAssets` from multiple goroutines (e.g. a `t.Parallel`/`sync.WaitGroup` test runnable under `-race`). Without such a test, a future refactor can silently reintroduce the unsynchronized access.
